crates/protocol/chio-provider-adapter-co: Shared external JSON helper checks original byte limits, duplicate keys and I-JSON before typed projection; argument objects and appended fragments have a 1 MiB cap. This is a parser, not an authentication capability.

All original SSE frames and assembled calls validate before any evaluator callback. A successful choice finish and configured transport terminator are separate conditions; errors deny before byte forwarding.
Choice/call identity is stable across bounded fragments. Provider errors, unfinished choices, trailing data, reused call IDs and ambiguous nested JSON reject before projection/evaluation.
crates/protocol/chio-bedrock-converse-ad: Every original SDK response body is collected under an actual-byte cap and strict validated before exposing any data frame to SDK decoding. This prevents SDK Value/Document projection from erasing duplicate keys.
crates/protocol/chio-provider-conformanc: Fixtures are bounded regular UTF-8 files with final-component nofollow/nonblocking opens on Unix. Native I/O and parser causes survive. Hostile concurrent ancestor replacement is outside this file helper contract.
Recorder network capture uses shared bounded reqwest transport and strict UTF-8; credentials are header values, not process argv. Status failures do not retain or echo provider response bodies.

AWS CLI stdout and stderr drain concurrently under independent byte caps and one total deadline. Capture owns and terminates its Unix process group on success and failure, including descendants that close inherited pipes. It is not a sandbox against descendants that deliberately leave the process group.

Anthropic capture reconstructs bounded final argument fragments and complete message lifecycle before creating fixture invocations; duplicate keys, IDs and mixed start/delta inputs reject. This pure reconstruction grants no authorization.
crates/protocol/chio-cohere-tools-adapte: The existing assembled-event Cohere contract consumes strict bounded SSE frames and typed tool blocks. All invocations prepare before evaluation, with a call-count cap and admitted registry sidecars; this does not add a new live delta-event protocol implementation.
crates/protocol/chio-gemini-tools-adapte: Existing whole-function-call Gemini chunks consume strict bounded SSE input; all invocations prepare before evaluation with a call-count cap and admitted registry sidecars. Provider-specific candidate extraction remains its own protocol contract.
